Show HN: Hyper Elements – Agents build emails, PDFs, images with 70% less tokens
items.summary: We built Hyper Elements. A open source content engine for agents. It lets them build emails, PDFs or images in React using much fewer tokens. The agent writes content, our engine handles the layout and markup. It also tells the agent what the problems are in the content and how to fix them. We tested it by giving Claude Code a brief and run it 5 times with different libraries like Hyper Elements, React Email and MJML. Each run, Hyper Elements used fewer tokens and produced a passing email much faster. The benchmark is also open source in the repo.

items.title: Show HN: Reylo – Import .sql files into TypeScript with full type inference
items.summary: Colin here, mostly known for creating Zod. Reylo is a new open source project I'm working on that takes advantage of the new Content Mapper API in TypeScript 7.1 (currently still in beta). Content mappers are sort of like plugins for TypeScript in that they let you define loaders for external file types. My mind went straight to .sql. This started as an experiment, but it's turned into a serious engineering effort. • Support for Postgres, MySQL, and SQLite • The inference engine is written in Rust. It relies on prepared queries to the greatest extent possible but augments from there with its own AST. • The major JSON schema extensions for each dialect are natively supported (e.g. pg_jsonschema on Postgres), so JSON Schema CHECK constraints are reflected in the return types • Type information bubbles up through JSON aggregation • We have our own internal type definition spec ("Reylo Type Defs") that's sort of like JSON Schema but it can represent a superset of the type systems in all major RDBMSs. Still just an internal representation, but there are a lot of fun ideas in it for anyone who's interested in that kind of design space. • Planning to add support for other languages beyond TypeScript soon, including a macro for Rust/sqlx Docs are here[0] or you can play around with the inference in-browser using the playground[1] (locally runs PGlite and Reylo's WASM build). [0] https://reylo.dev/docs [1] https://reylo.dev/play

items.title: Show HN: Wakeshift – Open-Source MCP Events for Claude Code, Codex and More
items.summary: tl;dr: We just open-sourced Wakeshift, which lets any MCP server serve interoperable events via MCP Events or harness-specific bridges. This allows MCP servers to push events to harnesses that don't support MCP Events today, including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Hi folks! The MCP Events spec was approved and merged five days ago, allowing MCP servers to emit events directly to agent subscribers. ( https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol... ) This allows MCP developers to push events directly to agents for long-running tasks (e.g. CI, crawls, starting agents) or external actions (e.g. emails, human approvals, alerts). However, the catch is that support for MCP Events is very light. Claude Code and Codex don't support it at all, and most of the implementations support the draft version rather than the merged spec. Many harnesses can work around this with plugins or hooks, but every MCP server has to build it for each harness. Wakeshift provides interoperable events to your MCP server. You call emit() and Wakeshift pushes the event to each subscribed agent in whatever format they accept: per the MCP Events final spec, an earlier draft, or through a hook / plugin where needed. If the harness requires a hook / plugin and it's not already installed, the agent will be notified and receive instructions on how to install it for the user. Additionally, the MCP Events spec defines three delivery mechanisms: webhook, push (via held HTTP request) and pull (via HTTP polling). The Wakeshift SDK serves push and poll from your MCP server, so agents that can't accept inbound HTTP webhooks (e.g. most agents running on laptops) can still get events within seconds. Subscriptions only start when an agent calls a tool that subscribes it, and users can list or stop them anytime. Some harnesses can only be woken by putting a message into the conversation, so Wakeshift wraps the content as an external event to reduce the risk of prompt injection. The repo linked has a quickstart guide to get this working locally in a few minutes. Or you can try our hosted webhook service to test it yourself without an installation. ( https://try.wakeshift.ai ) We'd love feedback, PRs for harnesses we don't cover, reports when it doesn't work. As you can imagine, there's a combinatorial explosion of servers, harnesses, models, OSs, etc. so we expect there to be some rough edges. Are there any MCP servers you're using that you think could benefit from having events today?

Show HN: I've become the dumb one, so I made a shortcut to ask Claude
items.summary: Whenever Claude hands a step back to me, a signup, onboarding or an API key Im lost; and most of the time stuck. No context, stuck on something easy. Me and Claude have switched seats quite fast: claude does the work and I'm the one who needs to be told what to do. And speed matters now. I have Claude Code sessions running all day, so I made one shortcut. Control-Option-A sends the window I'm looking at to a session and the answer shows up next to my work. I use it for everything now, not just the steps Claude gives me. Reading something, on X, on YouTube, one shortcut and I get an answer. Right now is Mac & Claude Code only, free and open source.
